page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v5 is an entry-level general-purpose instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of up to 3.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core using simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning stands at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates cryptographic instruction set support such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AVX extensions, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions.

Unlike cloud instances reliant entirely on network volumes, the D2ads_v5 integrates 81 GB of local SSD storage, suitable for temporary caches, scratch space, and swap files. It is also compatible with Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads requiring enterprise durability. The virtual machine does not include discrete GPU accelerators, orienting its resource envelope entirely around CPU execution and local disk I/O. It provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or external IP assignment for direct internet connectivity.

Benchmark evaluations emphasize a divide between single-thread responsiveness and overall aggregate throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the AMD processor achieves strong performance, ranking within the top 25 percent. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression likewise reach mid-range execution rates, complemented by a Geekbench single-core score of 1498.0. Conversely, aggregate multi-core tests, including Geekbench multi-core at 1836.0 and PassMark CPU at 3124.4, place the instance in the lower percentiles due to thread limits. Memory bandwidth remains constrained, measuring 33.13 GB/sec on uncached large reads and 22.28 GB/sec on writes, which restricts throughput on data-heavy tests such as PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations.

The primary architectural trade-off of the D2ads_v5 lies in its constrained compute footprint against its dedicated core quality and included local solid-state storage. While high-concurrency tasks, compilation pipelines, and high-volume database engines saturate the two available threads, the balanced memory allocation and integrated SSD provide solid operational density. The instance serves as an efficient operational tier for staging environments, containerized microservices, lightweight web serving, automated background scripts, and continuous integration runners with modest parallelization needs.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.7 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via multithreading, coupled with 8 GB of system memory and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes 81 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage, operating without discrete GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the host exhibits strong single-core execution alongside moderate compression throughput, though multi-threaded benchmarks, memory bandwidth, and database transaction rates reflect its modest two-thread capacity. From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the configuration delivers a cost-effective operational base for lightweight general-purpose computing where rapid temporary local storage is required, making it well matched for minor web services, batch scripting, microservices, and small development or test environments.
